solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: React badly with nannies perhaps wrapping heavy clothing

indicators.note: wrapping says the nannies' word goes round the rearranged letters

parts.note: nanny goats are female goats, so nannies are an example of goats

indicators.note: doing something badly scrambles it, so the letters of React are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone reacts poorly when the nannies arrive bundled up in heavy winter clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: The nannies are not childminders but female goats; 'badly' makes REATC, which 'wrapping' encloses.
explanation.definitionFit: Long thick overcoats worn by soldiers and in cold weather are heavy clothing.

clue.text: Dry up in company of the Queen

parts.note: being in company of someone is being with them
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword shorthand for the Queen

explanation.surface: Someone's enthusiasm fades away whenever they find themselves with the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Plants that dry up shrivel and fade, a direct synonym for the verb.

clue.text: What might guy I served with tart leave (if he liked it)?

definitions.text: What might guy I served with tart leave (if he liked it)?

indicators.note: served up here means presented in a new form, so these letters are dished out rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A waiter wonders what the diner they brought the tart to will leave if satisfied.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served' rearranges the letters of GUY I and TART together; the whole clue is also the definition, a diner's tip.
explanation.definitionFit: A tip left for a waiter by a satisfied customer is a voluntary payment for service.

clue.text: How Wise Men interpreted star attribute

definitions.meaning: the Magi read the star of Bethlehem as a portent
to attribute something is to ascribe or allot it

explanation.surface: The Magi read the Bethlehem star as a symbol to be attributed meaning.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading splits the answer into two words, AS SIGN.
explanation.definitionFit: To attribute a cause or blame to someone is to ascribe or allot it to them.

clue.text: Police officer, for example, turned up holding complete weapon

indicators.note: holding says the turned letters go round the next pieces
in a down clue turned up means the letters read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to end something is to complete it
an arm is a weapon, as in firearms

explanation.surface: A policeman is shown to have, say, flipped a fully loaded gun upward.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'turned up' reads bottom to top, giving GE; 'holding' wraps it round the complete weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: A French police officer, especially one in the military-run national force, is called this.

clue.text: Purple swelling with base coming to head

indicators.note: the base, or bottom letter, of a down entry moves up to the top

parts.note: a lump is a swelling on the body

explanation.surface: A purple bump on someone's skin has spread from its base up to the head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with base coming to head' takes the last letter P of LUMP to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A dark reddish-purple colour is named after the fruit of that shade.

clue.text: Minister outwardly admits lapse that is less sober

indicators.note: admits says those outer letters let the next pieces in
outwardly says only the outside letters of Minister are used

parts.note: to err is to lapse or make a mistake
IE, id est, is the abbreviation for 'that is'

explanation.surface: A clergyman confesses to a slip, implying he was not entirely sober.
explanation.walkthrough: The Minister is a clergyman in the surface but only lends its outer letters ('outwardly'), which 'admits' opens up.
explanation.definitionFit: Merrier is a comparative for tipsier, more cheerfully drunk, so less sober.

clue.text: Post-nuclear effect involving airborne fungal spores?

definitions.meaning: the billowing column that rises after an atomic blast
read literally, a cloud of spores released from toadstools floating in the air

explanation.surface: An atomic explosion's aftermath is compared to a puff of spores from a fungus.
explanation.definitionFit: The rising column after a nuclear explosion is shaped like a toadstool; read literally it is a cloud from a fungus.

clue.text: A woman will account for varnish

parts.note: a woman will contracts to 'she'll'

explanation.surface: A woman will pay for the varnish on the bill.
explanation.definitionFit: A resin dissolved in alcohol and used as a varnish for wood and furniture.

clue.text: Abandoned, once forty, nice sweet things

indicators.note: abandoned means wild and unrestrained, so the words that follow are rearranged freely

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone who, once forty, gave up the pleasant sweet treats they used to enjoy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Abandoned' rearranges ONCE, FORTY and NICE together.
explanation.definitionFit: Candies, chocolates and other sugary treats sold by a sweetshop are sweet things.

clue.text: Fare that's stranded in rank past eight

indicators.note: to rank things is to arrange them, so these letters are put into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Food is left stranded on a rank, waiting past eight o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in rank' rearranges PAST and EIGHT. 'stranded' means made of strands, not left stuck.
explanation.definitionFit: Long thin strands of pasta make this a food that comes in strings.

clue.text: Protest against new fiend

indicators.note: against means next to, so the protest leans on the new piece

parts.note: a demo is a protest march

explanation.surface: Demonstrators protest against a newly arrived evil spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: An evil spirit or devil is a fiend; the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Truce remains partially withdrawn — come again?

indicators.note: withdrawn says the hidden letters are read backwards
partially says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A ceasefire is partly holding; will the fighting break out again?
explanation.walkthrough: 'partially' picks RUCER from tRUCE Remains and 'withdrawn' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: To happen again or repeatedly is the sense; something that returns comes again.

clue.text: Means of getting around central London, perhaps essential for cyclists under pressure?

definitions.text: Means of getting around central London, perhaps
definitions.meaning: read as two words, a central (inner) underground train line, the Tube being London's underground
the inflatable rubber ring inside a bicycle tyre, kept under air pressure

explanation.surface: Cycling in central London under stress seems to need the Underground.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tube is London's underground railway; 'under pressure' refers to the inflated tyre, not stressed riders.
explanation.definitionFit: The inflatable rubber ring inside a bicycle tyre holds the air that keeps it firm.

clue.text: Flying away from settlement?

explanation.surface: An aircraft heading off far from any town.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally aloft, airborne; figuratively undecided, with a matter not yet resolved.

clue.text: Obstruction of light work by a financial district

parts.note: OP, short for opus, means a work
the City is London's financial district

explanation.surface: A building project in the banking district is blocking out the sunlight.
explanation.walkthrough: The City is the square mile of London that holds its banks.
explanation.definitionFit: Opaqueness, the quality of not letting light pass through, is the obstruction of light.

clue.text: Unassailable as one leaves sarcastic youth?

indicators.note: leaves says the letter for one departs from the words before it

parts.note: an ironic remark is a sarcastic one
I is the Roman numeral for one
a lad is a youth

explanation.surface: A mocking young man becomes unbeatable once someone goes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' takes one I out of IRONICLAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Armour-plated, so beyond attack; an argument this armoured cannot be challenged.

clue.text: Cultivated exotics get on reasonably well

indicators.note: plants that are cultivated are worked over, so the letters of the next word are reworked

explanation.surface: Foreign plants grown side by side manage to get along tolerably.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cultivated' rearranges EXOTICS.
explanation.definitionFit: Living side by side peacefully, tolerating each other, is getting on reasonably well.

clue.text: Fail to impress, appealing to receive base coin

indicators.note: to receive says the appealing word takes in the jumbled letters

parts.note: something cute is appealing

indicators.note: base coin is debased, so the word coin is corrupted into a different order

explanation.surface: Someone charming who accepts a counterfeit coin hardly impresses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'base' looks like a counterfeit coin but is the anagram signal, making NOIC; 'to receive' sets it inside.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom meaning to make no impression or have no effect on someone.

clue.text: I have out-of-this-world travel expense consuming my French gold

indicators.note: consuming says the expense word swallows the next pieces

parts.note: a cost is an expense
mon is the French word for my
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A traveller to space boasts of an expense eating into their French gold.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads as the traveller speaking in the first person; 'consuming' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A Russian space traveller is someone whose journey goes beyond Earth.

clue.text: Insist upon a lock-up

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the letters are read from the bottom

parts.note: a lock of hair is a tress

explanation.surface: Someone demands to be given a garage or storage unit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lock-up' looks like one word, a garage, but splits: a lock of hair read 'up' the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To declare firmly, maintain or state forcefully is to insist upon something.

clue.text: Paving prepared with edges of iroko

parts.note: knowing something off pat means having it prepared and ready

indicators.note: edges of says only the first and last letters of iroko are taken

explanation.surface: Paving made ready and trimmed with hardwood from the iroko tree.
explanation.walkthrough: Iroko is an African hardwood; 'edges of' gives its I and O.
explanation.definitionFit: A paved outdoor area beside a house is a terrace, so paving stands for it.

clue.text: Tree from the ends of the earth with soft interior

indicators.note: interior says the soft letter goes inside the other word

parts.note: the poles are the ends of the earth, so the polar regions
p, piano, is the musical abbreviation for soft

explanation.surface: A tree from the remotest regions with a soft inner core.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interior' is the container signal; P for soft comes from music notation.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall fast-growing deciduous tree of the willow family, a direct example.

clue.text: One dispenses with standard measures to elect one conservative

parts.note: to opt is to choose or elect
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone does away with the usual rules in order to vote for a Tory.
explanation.walkthrough: In a pub an optic is the device on an upturned bottle that pours fixed tots of spirit; 'dispenses with' means pours out, not does without.
explanation.definitionFit: A bar device fixed to a spirits bottle releases set measures, a fixed-amount dispenser.

clue.text: Piece of apparatus known for sharp projection

indicators.note: Piece of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Part of a well-known device is known for jutting out sharply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piece of' picks the letters from apparaTUS Known; 'for' links the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An elephant's long pointed ivory tooth sticks out sharply from the mouth.

clue.text: Exhibit western epic shot in Oxford, say

indicators.note: in says these pieces go inside the shoe word

parts.note: an Oxford is a style of lace-up shoe

indicators.note: shot means ruined or wrecked, so the letters of epic are jumbled

explanation.surface: A cowboy epic filmed in the university city of Oxford goes on display.
explanation.walkthrough: Oxford is not the city but a lace-up shoe; 'shot' makes PIEC, and 'in' sets it with W inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A prized item put on display as the finest example is an exhibit.

clue.text: Religious instruction niche in church had turned to hopelessness

indicators.note: turned says the combined pieces are read backwards

parts.note: RI is the school abbreviation for religious instruction
an apse is a recess at the east end of a church
'd is the contracted form of had

explanation.surface: A scripture lesson held in a church recess had sunk into gloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' reverses RIAPSED.
explanation.definitionFit: Loss of all hope, utter hopelessness, is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Suspicious about the thing producing generous impulse

indicators.note: about says the suspicious word surrounds the next piece

parts.note: chary means wary or suspicious
it stands for the thing

explanation.surface: Being wary of something can still lead to kindness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the container signal; 'producing' only links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Kindness and goodwill toward others, especially in giving, is a generous impulse.
